title: Delphi: the oracle's voice

lines.text: Hi! This is a MyCast demo. Today we climb to Delphi, on the slope of Mount Parnassus.
Where the Greeks went to ask about the future. Why there?
The Greeks thought Delphi was the centre of the world. A stone called the omphalos, the navel, marked the spot.
Lovely. And who gave the answers?
Apollo's priestess, the Pythia. People came to her with big decisions from all over the ancient world: cities, kings and ordinary people.
Where does the name Pythia come from?
The place was once called Pytho. In the myth a serpent, Python, lived here until Apollo killed it. Hence the Pythia.
I have heard the oracle's answers could be ambiguous.
The most famous example comes from Herodotus. King Croesus of Lydia asked whether to make war on Persia. The answer: if he did, he would destroy a great empire.
His own. Ancient tradition also says the temple of Apollo bore the words: Know thyself.
Advice that has not aged. And what about Delphi today?
The sanctuary declined in late antiquity, and French archaeologists excavated it from the late nineteenth century. Today it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
And people still go there, now looking for answers of their own.
That was a MyCast demo episode. You can build your own podcast at mycast.pro.
